[LLM] Python backdoor self-daemonisation via __DAEMONIZED=1 spawned by VS Code helper or node Installation Medium
The Nx Console v18.95.0 macOS backdoor re-execs itself with __DAEMONIZED=1 in its environment to detach from the VS Code extension host parent — a distinctive marker used by cat.py. This UC hunts python processes spawned by code/cursor/node/shell parents that either run cat.py from the kitty directory or carry the __DAEMONIZED=1 token in their command-line / parent command-line. Rationale: The __DAEMONIZED=1 environment-variable self-relaunch is a distinctive marker called out by the GitHub Security Advisory and StepSecurity writeup for the cat.py backdoor — legitimate Python tooling does not use this sentinel. Combining it with the kitty/cat.py path and a VS Code helper / node / shell parent yields high fidelity. Cross-checked against GHSA-c9j4-9m59-847w and StepSecurity IOC list. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/nrwl/nx-console/security/advisories/GHSA-c9j4-9m59-847w • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/nx-console-vs-code-extension-compromised • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/compromised-nx-console-18950-targeted.html
ATT&CKT1059.006 T1564.012 T1036.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName in~ ("python","python3","python3.9","python3.10","python3.11","python3.12","python.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("cat.py","/.local/share/kitty/","/tmp/kitty-","__DAEMONIZED=1")
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("__DAEMONIZED=1","cat.py","/.local/share/kitty/")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node","node.exe","Code Helper","Code Helper (Plugin)","Code","Cursor","cursor-helper","sh","zsh","bash","python","python3")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, ProcessId, InitiatingProcessId
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ActingProcessName matches regex @"(?i)(^|/)python(3(\.[0-9]+)?)?(\.exe)?$"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("cat.py","/.local/share/kitty/","/tmp/kitty-","__DAEMONIZED=1")
   or ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("__DAEMONIZED=1","cat.py")
| where ParentProcessName in~ ("node","Code Helper","Code Helper (Plugin)","Code","Cursor","cursor-helper","sh","zsh","bash","python","python3")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] VS Code extension host fan-out reads of developer secrets (.ssh, .aws, .npmrc, ~/.claude/settings.json) Actions on Objectives Medium
The poisoned Nx Console payload sweeps developer credentials from a fixed list — SSH private keys, AWS credentials, npm tokens, Claude Code config (~/.claude/settings.json — believed to be the first supply-chain payload to target an AI assistant config), gcloud, kube, gnupg, docker, and .env files. This UC alerts when the VS Code / Cursor extension-host Node process touches ≥4 distinct credential-bearing paths within a 10-minute window — a shape no legitimate extension exhibits. Rationale: Anchors on the exact credential-file list disclosed by the GitHub Security Advisory and StepSecurity for the cat.py / Nx Console payload, including the novel target ~/.claude/settings.json that the article calls out as one of the first AI-assistant config harvest behaviours seen in the wild. The ≥4-distinct-paths threshold within 10 minutes is a sweep marker that no legitimate VS Code extension exhibits. Cross-checked GHSA-c9j4-9m59-847w + StepSecurity + The Hacker News. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/nrwl/nx-console/security/advisories/GHSA-c9j4-9m59-847w • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/nx-console-vs-code-extension-compromised • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/compromised-nx-console-18950-targeted.html • https://cybersecuritynews.com/nx-console-vs-code-extension-compromised/
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1552.004 T1083
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileAccessed","FileRead","FileOpened")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node","node.exe","Code Helper","Code Helper (Plugin)","cursor-helper","Cursor","Code","code.exe","cursor.exe","python","python3")
| where (FolderPath has_any ("/.ssh/","/.aws/","/.config/gcloud/","/.kube/","/.docker/","/.gnupg/","/.claude/")
     or FileName in~ ("id_rsa","id_ed25519","id_ecdsa","credentials","known_hosts","authorized_keys",".npmrc","settings.json","config.json")
     or FileName =~ ".env" or FileName startswith ".env." or FolderPath has "/.npmrc")
| where not (FolderPath has "/.claude/" and FileName != "settings.json")    // narrow .claude noise — only the settings.json file matters
| summarize PathCount = dcount(strcat(FolderPath, FileName)),
            Paths = make_set(strcat(FolderPath, FileName), 25),
            FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp)
            by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, bin(Timestamp, 10m)
| where PathCount >= 4    // 4 = sweep threshold; one-off .env read is normal dev work, ≥4 distinct cred files in 10 min is harvesting behaviour
| order by FirstSeen desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName in~ ("node","node.exe","Code Helper","Code Helper (Plugin)","cursor-helper","Cursor","Code","code.exe","cursor.exe","python","python3")
| where (TargetFilePath has_any ("/.ssh/","/.aws/","/.config/gcloud/","/.kube/","/.docker/","/.gnupg/","/.claude/")
     or TargetFileName in~ ("id_rsa","id_ed25519","id_ecdsa","credentials","known_hosts","authorized_keys",".npmrc")
     or TargetFileName =~ ".env" or TargetFileName startswith ".env."
     or (TargetFilePath has "/.claude/" and TargetFileName =~ "settings.json"))
| summarize PathCount = dcount(TargetFilePath),
            Paths = make_set(TargetFilePath, 25),
            FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 10m)
| where PathCount >= 4    // 4 = empirical sweep threshold
| order by FirstSeen desc
source:(linux.auditd OR windows.sysmon) (@process.name:(node OR python OR python3) OR @Image:(*\\node.exe OR *Code\ Helper* OR *cursor-helper* OR *\\Code.exe OR *\\Cursor.exe)) (@file.path:(*/.ssh/id_rsa OR */.ssh/id_ed25519 OR */.ssh/id_ecdsa OR */.aws/credentials OR */.aws/config OR */.npmrc OR */.config/gcloud/* OR */.kube/config OR */.docker/config.json OR */.gnupg/* OR */.claude/settings.json OR */.env OR */.env.*) OR @TargetFilename:(*\\.ssh\\id_rsa OR *\\.aws\\credentials OR *\\.npmrc OR *\\.claude\\settings.json OR *\\.env))
#event_simpleName=FileOpenInfo ContextImageFileName=/(node|Code Helper|cursor-helper|Cursor|Code|python3?)\.?(exe)?$/i
| (TargetFileName=/\/\.ssh\/(id_(rsa|ed25519|ecdsa)|known_hosts|config|authorized_keys)$/i OR TargetFileName=/\/\.aws\/(credentials|config)$/i OR TargetFileName=/\/\.npmrc$/i OR TargetFileName=/\/\.config\/gcloud\//i OR TargetFileName=/\/\.kube\/config$/i OR TargetFileName=/\/\.docker\/config\.json$/i OR TargetFileName=/\/\.gnupg\//i OR TargetFileName=/\/\.claude\/settings\.json$/i OR TargetFileName=/\/\.env(\.[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+)?$/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, bucket(span=10m)], function=[count(field=TargetFileName, distinct=true, as=PathCount), collect(TargetFileName, multival=true)])
| PathCount >= 4

Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs Actions on Objectives High
Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.
ATT&CKT1539 T1555.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",
                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",
                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:

logsource:

detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'

            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:

level: high

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")

title: Obfuscated / Encoded PowerShell Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d08
status: experimental
description: |
    PowerShell launched with -EncodedCommand, base64 strings, hidden
    window, no-profile, bypass policy, IEX / Invoke-Expression / Net
    .WebClient.DownloadString — combinations indicating evasion.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1027/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1027
    - attack.execution
    - attack.defense-evasion
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_image:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
    selection_args:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '-enc '
            - 'EncodedCommand'
            - 'FromBase64String'
            - 'Invoke-Expression'
            - 'IEX('
            - 'DownloadString'
            - 'Net.WebClient'
            - '-w hidden'
            - '-WindowStyle Hidden'
            - '-nop'
            - '-NoProfile'
            - '-ep bypass'
            - '-ExecutionPolicy Bypass'
    condition: selection_image and selection_args
falsepositives:
    - DevOps tooling that legitimately uses encoded command for
      cross-shell escaping
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1", "43f2b001846c4966073ebffa5be8f15e491a1e7d32bbd805d57406ff540e0dd9", "558b09d7ad0d1660e2a0fb8a06da81a6f42e06d2", "ba642fe2c7c65e42dd7f6444b83023dc6827e08c", "acfc3f957a63b4cde93ff645f2b6bf26a8ed1bbf", "9d88f040c44b5f4d5f9db15ff89310776c168e99") or SHA1 in~ ("1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1", "43f2b001846c4966073ebffa5be8f15e491a1e7d32bbd805d57406ff540e0dd9", "558b09d7ad0d1660e2a0fb8a06da81a6f42e06d2", "ba642fe2c7c65e42dd7f6444b83023dc6827e08c", "acfc3f957a63b4cde93ff645f2b6bf26a8ed1bbf", "9d88f040c44b5f4d5f9db15ff89310776c168e99") or MD5 in~ ("1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1", "43f2b001846c4966073ebffa5be8f15e491a1e7d32bbd805d57406ff540e0dd9", "558b09d7ad0d1660e2a0fb8a06da81a6f42e06d2", "ba642fe2c7c65e42dd7f6444b83023dc6827e08c", "acfc3f957a63b4cde93ff645f2b6bf26a8ed1bbf", "9d88f040c44b5f4d5f9db15ff89310776c168e99")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1", "43f2b001846c4966073ebffa5be8f15e491a1e7d32bbd805d57406ff540e0dd9", "558b09d7ad0d1660e2a0fb8a06da81a6f42e06d2", "ba642fe2c7c65e42dd7f6444b83023dc6827e08c", "acfc3f957a63b4cde93ff645f2b6bf26a8ed1bbf", "9d88f040c44b5f4d5f9db15ff89310776c168e99") or SHA1 in~ ("1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1", "43f2b001846c4966073ebffa5be8f15e491a1e7d32bbd805d57406ff540e0dd9", "558b09d7ad0d1660e2a0fb8a06da81a6f42e06d2", "ba642fe2c7c65e42dd7f6444b83023dc6827e08c", "acfc3f957a63b4cde93ff645f2b6bf26a8ed1bbf", "9d88f040c44b5f4d5f9db15ff89310776c168e99") or MD5 in~ ("1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1", "43f2b001846c4966073ebffa5be8f15e491a1e7d32bbd805d57406ff540e0dd9", "558b09d7ad0d1660e2a0fb8a06da81a6f42e06d2", "ba642fe2c7c65e42dd7f6444b83023dc6827e08c", "acfc3f957a63b4cde93ff645f2b6bf26a8ed1bbf", "9d88f040c44b5f4d5f9db15ff89310776c168e99")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1", "43f2b001846c4966073ebffa5be8f15e491a1e7d32bbd805d57406ff540e0dd9", "558b09d7ad0d1660e2a0fb8a06da81a6f42e06d2", "ba642fe2c7c65e42dd7f6444b83023dc6827e08c", "acfc3f957a63b4cde93ff645f2b6bf26a8ed1bbf", "9d88f040c44b5f4d5f9db15ff89310776c168e99"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Tracking TamperedChef Clusters via Certificate and Code Reuse

Unit 42 (Palo Alto)
2026-05-20 13 use cases 8 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

Unit 42 analyzes TamperedChef malware clusters that use trojanized productivity apps and malvertising to deliver stealthy payloads to targets. The post Tracking TamperedChef Clusters via Certificate and Code Reuse appeared first on Unit 42 .

ATT&CKT1027 T1053.005 T1176 T1190 T1204.002 T1547.001 T1555.003 T1649
Domainscrystalpdf.com vault.appsuites.ai pdf-tool.appsuites.ai appsuites.ai freeonlinetools.info

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Tracking TamperedChef Clusters via Certificate and Code Reuse
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] TamperedChef shell-company code-signing certificate execution (CL-UNK-1090) · [LLM] TamperedChef trojanized-app activation via --cm / --enableupdate / --fullupdate flags · [LLM] TamperedChef scheduled-task persistence via task.xml + obfuscated JS (appsuite-print.js) · Suspicious browser extension installation · Scheduled task created with suspicious image / encoded args
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] TamperedChef C2 / distribution callback to appsuites.ai and sibling domains · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs
[LLM] TamperedChef shell-company code-signing certificate execution (CL-UNK-1090) Installation High
Hunts execution of binaries signed by the five disposable LLCs Unit 42 attributes to the CL-UNK-1090 TamperedChef cluster: CANDY TECH LTD, G.R.CIGAR. LTD, TAU CENTAURI LTD, AMARYLLIS SIGNAL LTD, METROPOLITAN DESIGN LLC. These shell entities exist solely to obtain Authenticode certs for trojanized PDF/recipe/calendar productivity apps; legitimate software from these company names does not exist. Rationale: The five LLC signer strings come directly from the Unit 42 table mapping CL-UNK-1090 binaries to their shell-company signers. These names are unique to the cluster and don't appear in legitimate software publishers. Confirmed against Sophos and WithSecure reporting that the operators rotate cert-issuing LLCs. Cross-checked against: • https://www.sophos.com/en-us/blog/tamperedchef-serves-bad-ads-with-infostealers-as-the-main-course • https://labs.withsecure.com/publications/tamperedchef • https://www.acronis.com/en/tru/posts/cooking-up-trouble-how-tamperedchef-uses-signed-apps-to-deliver-stealthy-payloads/
ATT&CKT1588.003 T1036.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
let TamperedChefSigners = dynamic(["CANDY TECH LTD","G.R.CIGAR. LTD","G.R.CIGAR LTD","TAU CENTAURI LTD","AMARYLLIS SIGNAL LTD","METROPOLITAN DESIGN LLC"]);
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ProcessVersionInfoCompanyName in~ (TamperedChefSigners)
   or InitiatingProcessVersionInfoCompanyName in~ (TamperedChefSigners)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
          Signer = coalesce(ProcessVersionInfoCompanyName, InitiatingProcessVersionInfoCompanyName),
          Product = ProcessVersionInfoProductName,
          ProcessCommandLine,
          ParentFileName = InitiatingProcessFileName,
          ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
let TamperedChefSigners = dynamic(["CANDY TECH LTD","G.R.CIGAR. LTD","G.R.CIGAR LTD","TAU CENTAURI LTD","AMARYLLIS SIGNAL LTD","METROPOLITAN DESIGN LLC"]);
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ActingProcessFileCompany in~ (TamperedChefSigners)
   or ParentProcessFileCompany in~ (TamperedChefSigners)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine,
          Signer = coalesce(ActingProcessFileCompany, ParentProcessFileCompany),
          Product = ActingProcessFileProduct,
          SHA256, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] TamperedChef C2 / distribution callback to appsuites.ai and sibling domains Command & Control High
Hunts host network egress and DNS to the article's named TamperedChef infrastructure: appsuites.ai (including pdf-tool / vault subdomains), crystalpdf.com, freeonlinetools.info. These are the trojanized-installer download hosts and the dormant-then-activate C2 used by CL-CRI-1089 / CL-UNK-1090. Rationale: appsuites.ai, pdf-tool.appsuites.ai, vault.appsuites.ai, crystalpdf.com and freeonlinetools.info are the article's named distribution/C2 hosts; fullpdf.com added from Sophos corroboration. These are unique campaign-specific domains — no legitimate business overlap. Any callback after the dormancy window is high-confidence post-install activation. Cross-checked against: • https://www.sophos.com/en-us/blog/tamperedchef-serves-bad-ads-with-infostealers-as-the-main-course • https://thehackernews.com/2025/08/tamperedchef-malware-disguised-as-fake.html • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/tamperedchef-infostealer-delivered-through-fraudulent-pdf-editor/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1568 T1105
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Web.Web Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
let TamperedChefHosts = dynamic(["appsuites.ai","pdf-tool.appsuites.ai","vault.appsuites.ai","crystalpdf.com","freeonlinetools.info","fullpdf.com"]);
let NetHits = DeviceNetworkEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where isnotempty(RemoteUrl)
  | extend Host = tolower(tostring(parse_url(RemoteUrl).Host))
  | where Host in~ (TamperedChefHosts) or Host endswith ".appsuites.ai" or Host endswith ".crystalpdf.com"
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, Source = "Network", Indicator = RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessVersionInfoCompanyName;
let DnsHits = DeviceEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where ActionType == "DnsQueryResponse"
  | extend Query = tolower(tostring(parse_json(AdditionalFields).DnsQueryString))
  | where Query in~ (TamperedChefHosts) or Query endswith ".appsuites.ai" or Query endswith ".crystalpdf.com"
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, Source = "DNS", Indicator = Query, RemoteIP = tostring(parse_json(AdditionalFields).IPAddresses), InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessVersionInfoCompanyName;
union NetHits, DnsHits
| order by Timestamp desc
let TamperedChefHosts = dynamic(["appsuites.ai","pdf-tool.appsuites.ai","vault.appsuites.ai","crystalpdf.com","freeonlinetools.info","fullpdf.com"]);
ImDnsActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DnsQuery in~ (TamperedChefHosts) or DnsQuery endswith ".appsuites.ai" or DnsQuery endswith ".crystalpdf.com"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, DnsQuery, EventVendor, EventProduct
| union (
    CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where RequestURL has_any (TamperedChefHosts) or DestinationHostName has_any (TamperedChefHosts)
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname = SourceHostName, SrcIpAddr = SourceIP, SrcUsername = SourceUserName, DnsQuery = coalesce(DestinationHostName, RequestURL), EventVendor = DeviceVendor, EventProduct = DeviceProduct
  )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] TamperedChef trojanized-app activation via --cm / --enableupdate / --fullupdate flags Installation High
Hunts the article's productivity-app installers (AppSuite, CrystalPDF, Calendaromatic, JustAskJacky) re-launching themselves with the activation flags --cm, --install, --enableupdate or --fullupdate. These flags are the documented switch from dormant-installed state to active stealer/C2 behaviour and have no legitimate productivity-software analogue. Rationale: Article names AppSuite PDF, Calendaromatic, JustAskJacky and CrystalPDF as the trojanized productivity apps. Sophos/Acronis/SecurityOnline corroborate --cm as the documented activation argument and --enableupdate / --fullupdate / --install as the persistent-update flags; these strings don't appear in legitimate productivity-app installers and pair directly with the article's family. Cross-checked against: • https://www.sophos.com/en-us/blog/tamperedchef-serves-bad-ads-with-infostealers-as-the-main-course • https://securityonline.info/tamperedchef-malware-rises-deceptive-apps-use-signed-binaries-and-seo-poisoning-to-hijack-browsers/ • https://www.acronis.com/en/tru/posts/cooking-up-trouble-how-tamperedchef-uses-signed-apps-to-deliver-stealthy-payloads/
ATT&CKT1059 T1204.002 T1480
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
let TamperedChefBinaries = dynamic(["AppSuitePDF.exe","AppSuite.exe","CrystalPDF.exe","Calendaromatic.exe","JustAskJacky.exe","PDFEditor.exe","ManualFinder.exe","RecipeLister.exe","OneStart.exe","EpiBrowser.exe"]);
let TamperedChefSigners = dynamic(["CANDY TECH LTD","G.R.CIGAR. LTD","G.R.CIGAR LTD","TAU CENTAURI LTD","AMARYLLIS SIGNAL LTD","METROPOLITAN DESIGN LLC"]);
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName in~ (TamperedChefBinaries)
   or ProcessVersionInfoCompanyName in~ (TamperedChefSigners)
   or ProcessVersionInfoProductName has_any ("AppSuite","CrystalPDF","Calendaromatic","JustAskJacky","Recipe Lister","Manual Finder")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("--cm ","--cm=","--enableupdate","--fullupdate","--install ")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256,
          Signer = ProcessVersionInfoCompanyName,
          Product = ProcessVersionInfoProductName,
          ParentFileName = InitiatingProcessFileName,
          ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
let TamperedChefBinaries = dynamic(["AppSuitePDF.exe","AppSuite.exe","CrystalPDF.exe","Calendaromatic.exe","JustAskJacky.exe","PDFEditor.exe","ManualFinder.exe","RecipeLister.exe","OneStart.exe","EpiBrowser.exe"]);
let TamperedChefSigners = dynamic(["CANDY TECH LTD","G.R.CIGAR. LTD","G.R.CIGAR LTD","TAU CENTAURI LTD","AMARYLLIS SIGNAL LTD","METROPOLITAN DESIGN LLC"]);
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where tostring(ActingProcessName) in~ (TamperedChefBinaries)
   or ActingProcessFileCompany in~ (TamperedChefSigners)
   or ActingProcessFileProduct has_any ("AppSuite","CrystalPDF","Calendaromatic","JustAskJacky","Recipe Lister","Manual Finder")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("--cm ","--cm=","--enableupdate","--fullupdate","--install ")
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, SHA256,
          Signer = ActingProcessFileCompany,
          Product = ActingProcessFileProduct,
          ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: TamperedChef Productivity-App Activation Flags
id: 6c3e8a2d-4d6b-4cad-bf5c-7b3c4d5e6f7a
description: Detects TamperedChef trojanized productivity apps (AppSuite, CrystalPDF, Calendaromatic, JustAskJacky) launching with documented activation/update flags --cm, --enableupdate, --fullupdate, --install.
references:
  - https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/tracking-tampered-chef-clusters/
  - https://securityonline.info/tamperedchef-malware-rises-deceptive-apps-use-signed-binaries-and-seo-poisoning-to-hijack-browsers/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/20
tags:
  - attack.t1059
  - attack.t1204.002
  - attack.t1480
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_image:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\AppSuitePDF.exe'
      - '\AppSuite.exe'
      - '\CrystalPDF.exe'
      - '\Calendaromatic.exe'
      - '\JustAskJacky.exe'
      - '\PDFEditor.exe'
      - '\ManualFinder.exe'
      - '\RecipeLister.exe'
  selection_flags:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '--cm '
      - '--cm='
      - '--enableupdate'
      - '--fullupdate'
      - '--install '
  condition: selection_image and selection_flags
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 (@Image:(*\\AppSuite*.exe OR *\\CrystalPDF.exe OR *\\Calendaromatic.exe OR *\\JustAskJacky.exe OR *\\appsuite*.exe OR *\\crystalpdf.exe OR *\\calendaromatic.exe OR *\\justaskjacky.exe)) (@CommandLine:*--cm* OR @CommandLine:*--enableupdate* OR @CommandLine:*--fullupdate* OR @CommandLine:*--install*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ImageFileName=/(AppSuite(PDF)?|CrystalPDF|Calendaromatic|JustAskJacky|PDFEditor|ManualFinder|RecipeLister)\.exe$/i
| CommandLine=/(--cm[=\s]|--enableupdate|--fullupdate|--install\s)/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, SHA256HashData], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmdline values(Processes.parent_process_name) as parent values(Processes.process_hash) as hash from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name IN ("AppSuitePDF.exe","CrystalPDF.exe","Calendaromatic.exe","JustAskJacky.exe","PDFEditor.exe","ManualFinder.exe","RecipeLister.exe") OR Processes.process LIKE "%AppSuite%" OR Processes.process LIKE "%CrystalPDF%") AND (Processes.process LIKE "%--cm %" OR Processes.process LIKE "%--cm\"%" OR Processes.process LIKE "%--enableupdate%" OR Processes.process LIKE "%--fullupdate%" OR Processes.process LIKE "%--install %") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where firstTime >= relative_time(now(), "-30d@d")
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmdline values(Processes.parent_process_name) as parent values(Processes.process_hash) as hash from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name IN ("AppSuitePDF.exe","CrystalPDF.exe","Calendaromatic.exe","JustAskJacky.exe","PDFEditor.exe","ManualFinder.exe","RecipeLister.exe") OR Processes.process LIKE "%AppSuite%" OR Processes.process LIKE "%CrystalPDF%") AND (Processes.process LIKE "%--cm %" OR Processes.process LIKE "%--cm\"%" OR Processes.process LIKE "%--enableupdate%" OR Processes.process LIKE "%--fullupdate%" OR Processes.process LIKE "%--install %") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where firstTime >= relative_time(now(), "-30d@d")
[LLM] TamperedChef scheduled-task persistence via task.xml + obfuscated JS (appsuite-print.js) Installation High
Hunts the article-corroborated TamperedChef persistence pattern: schtasks.exe importing a freshly-dropped task.xml that registers a recurring task launching wscript/cscript against an obfuscated JS such as appsuite-print.js. Combines the file-drop, the schtasks /create /xml import and the resulting script-host execution to catch the persistence handoff. Rationale: task.xml drop + schtasks /create /xml + obfuscated JS (appsuite-print.js) is the TamperedChef persistence handoff documented by SecurityOnline and Acronis corroborating the article's CL-CRI-1089 trojanized-app behaviour. The 24h join window catches the schedule registration paired to the subsequent script-host launch, dramatically reducing FP vs schtasks alone. Cross-checked against: • https://securityonline.info/tamperedchef-malware-rises-deceptive-apps-use-signed-binaries-and-seo-poisoning-to-hijack-browsers/ • https://www.acronis.com/en/tru/posts/cooking-up-trouble-how-tamperedchef-uses-signed-apps-to-deliver-stealthy-payloads/ • https://www.sophos.com/en-us/blog/tamperedchef-serves-bad-ads-with-infostealers-as-the-main-course
ATT&CKT1053.005 T1059.007 T1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
let WindowHours = 24h;
let ScheduleHits = DeviceProcessEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where FileName =~ "schtasks.exe"
  | where ProcessCommandLine has_all ("/create","/xml")
  | where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("\\Temp\\","\\AppData\\","AppSuite","CrystalPDF","Calendaromatic","JustAskJacky","task.xml")
  | project SchedTime = Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
            SchedCmd = ProcessCommandLine,
            SchedParent = InitiatingProcessFileName,
            SchedParentCompany = InitiatingProcessVersionInfoCompanyName;
let ScriptHits = DeviceProcessEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where FileName in~ ("wscript.exe","cscript.exe","node.exe")
  | where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("appsuite-print.js","appsuite","crystalpdf","calendaromatic","justaskjacky") and ProcessCommandLine has ".js"
  | project ScriptTime = Timestamp, DeviceName, ScriptCmd = ProcessCommandLine,
            ScriptParent = InitiatingProcessFileName;
ScheduleHits
| join kind=inner ScriptHits on DeviceName
| where ScriptTime between (SchedTime .. SchedTime + WindowHours)
| project SchedTime, ScriptTime, DeviceName, AccountName,
          SchedParent, SchedParentCompany, SchedCmd,
          ScriptParent, ScriptCmd
| order by SchedTime desc
let WindowHours = 24h;
let ScheduleHits = ImProcessCreate
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where ActingProcessName endswith "schtasks.exe"
  | where ActingProcessCommandLine has_all ("/create","/xml")
  | where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("\\Temp\\","\\AppData\\","AppSuite","CrystalPDF","Calendaromatic","JustAskJacky","task.xml")
  | project SchedTime = TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
            SchedCmd = ActingProcessCommandLine,
            SchedParentName = ParentProcessName,
            SchedParentCompany = ParentProcessFileCompany;
let ScriptHits = ImProcessCreate
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where ActingProcessName endswith "wscript.exe" or ActingProcessName endswith "cscript.exe" or ActingProcessName endswith "node.exe"
  | where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("appsuite-print.js","appsuite","crystalpdf","calendaromatic","justaskjacky") and ActingProcessCommandLine has ".js"
  | project ScriptTime = TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ScriptCmd = ActingProcessCommandLine,
            ScriptParent = ParentProcessName;
ScheduleHits
| join kind=inner ScriptHits on DvcHostname
| where ScriptTime between (SchedTime .. SchedTime + WindowHours)
| project SchedTime, ScriptTime, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          SchedParentName, SchedParentCompany, SchedCmd,
          ScriptParent, ScriptCmd
| order by SchedTime desc
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 (@Image:(*\\schtasks.exe OR *\\SCHTASKS.EXE)) @CommandLine:(*"/create"* AND *"/xml"*) (@CommandLine:*task.xml* OR @CommandLine:*AppSuite* OR @CommandLine:*CrystalPDF* OR @CommandLine:*Calendaromatic* OR @CommandLine:*JustAskJacky* OR @CommandLine:*appsuite-print.js*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ImageFileName=/\\schtasks\.exe$/i
| regex("/create", field=CommandLine)
| regex("/xml", field=CommandLine)
| regex("(task\\.xml|AppSuite|CrystalPDF|Calendaromatic|JustAskJacky|appsuite-print\\.js)", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, CommandLine, ParentBaseFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmdline values(Processes.parent_process_name) as parent from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name="schtasks.exe" Processes.process="*/create*" Processes.process="*/xml*" (Processes.process LIKE "%\\Temp\\%task.xml%" OR Processes.process LIKE "%\\AppData\\%task.xml%" OR Processes.process LIKE "%AppSuite%task%.xml%" OR Processes.process LIKE "%CrystalPDF%task%.xml%") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where firstTime >= relative_time(now(), "-30d@d") | join type=outer dest [| tstats summariesonly=true count from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("wscript.exe","cscript.exe") (Processes.process LIKE "%appsuite-print.js%" OR Processes.process LIKE "%appsuite%.js%" OR Processes.process LIKE "%crystalpdf%.js%") by Processes.dest Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | rename process as script_cmdline]
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmdline values(Processes.parent_process_name) as parent from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name="schtasks.exe" Processes.process="*/create*" Processes.process="*/xml*" (Processes.process LIKE "%\\Temp\\%task.xml%" OR Processes.process LIKE "%\\AppData\\%task.xml%" OR Processes.process LIKE "%AppSuite%task%.xml%" OR Processes.process LIKE "%CrystalPDF%task%.xml%") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where firstTime >= relative_time(now(), "-30d@d") | join type=outer dest [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("wscript.exe","cscript.exe") (Processes.process LIKE "%appsuite-print.js%" OR Processes.process LIKE "%appsuite%.js%" OR Processes.process LIKE "%crystalpdf%.js%") by Processes.dest Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | rename process as script_cmdline]
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

DeviceNetworkEvents

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time

Command & Control
Detected
Phase 7
Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Article-specific behavioural hunt — GitHub breached via a malicious VS Code extension: why developer devices are the
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] TeamPCP Nx Console payload SHA256 hash match on developer endpoints · [LLM] VS Code child process fetching payload from nrwl/nx orphan commit (Nx Console v18.95.0 dropper) · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] DNS / Network egress to TeamPCP Nx Console C2 domain check.git-service.com · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Burst credential-file harvest by VS Code / node process (Nx Console stealer behaviour) · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs
[LLM] DNS / Network egress to TeamPCP Nx Console C2 domain check.git-service.com Command & Control High
Hunts any developer endpoint resolving or connecting to check.git-service.com (or sibling subdomains under git-service.com), the credential-exfiltration host used by the TeamPCP Nx Console v18.95.0 supply-chain payload. The domain has no legitimate use — any hit is high-fidelity for the GitHub-breach campaign. Rationale: Domain check.git-service.com is the article's lead IOC; cross-checked via BleepingComputer and StepSecurity write-ups of the same Nx Console v18.95.0 / TeamPCP incident. Any DNS query for this name from a corporate endpoint indicates active credential exfiltration in progress. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/nx-console-vs-code-extension-compromised • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/github-confirms-breach-of-3-800-repos-via-malicious-vscode-extension/ • https://github.com/nrwl/nx-console/security/advisories/GHSA-c9j4-9m59-847w • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/github-internal-repositories-breached.html

[LLM] TeamPCP Nx Console payload SHA256 hash match on developer endpoints Installation High
Direct hash-based detection for the four known Nx Console v18.95.0 malicious payload SHA256s — the 2,777-byte injected stub plus the dropped 498KB obfuscated stealer fetched from the nrwl/nx orphan commit. Any write or execution of these binaries on a corporate endpoint is unambiguous compromise. Rationale: Four SHA256s from the article's IOC block; campaign and payload behaviour cross-checked against the official nrwl/nx-console GHSA advisory and StepSecurity analysis. Hash matches on developer endpoints are unambiguous and warrant immediate isolation. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/nrwl/nx-console/security/advisories/GHSA-c9j4-9m59-847w • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/nx-console-vs-code-extension-compromised • https://nx.dev/blog/nx-console-v18-95-0-postmortem

[LLM] VS Code child process fetching payload from nrwl/nx orphan commit (Nx Console v18.95.0 dropper) Installation High
Detects the post-install execution chain unique to the TeamPCP Nx Console compromise: a child process of VS Code (Code.exe / Code - Insiders.exe) invoking npx, node, cmd, or PowerShell with a command line that references either the malicious orphan commit SHA 558b09d7ad0d1660e2a0fb8a06da81a6f42e06d2 or raw.githubusercontent.com/nrwl/nx — the exact mechanism that pulls down the 498KB obfuscated stealer. Rationale: Pivots on the unique orphan-commit SHA 558b09d7ad0d1660e2a0fb8a06da81a6f42e06d2 (confirmed by the nrwl/nx-console GHSA advisory and Nx postmortem) plus the raw.githubusercontent.com/nrwl/nx fetch pattern — both are second-source-verified and have no legitimate use. The parent=Code.exe + child=npx/node + URL pattern is unique to the Nx Console v18.95.0 activation flow. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/nrwl/nx-console/security/advisories/GHSA-c9j4-9m59-847w • https://nx.dev/blog/nx-console-v18-95-0-postmortem • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/nx-console-vs-code-extension-compromised
ATT&CKT1059.007 T1105 T1195.002 T1176

title: VS Code Child Process Fetching Nx Console v18.95.0 Stealer From nrwl/nx Orphan Commit

[LLM] Burst credential-file harvest by VS Code / node process (Nx Console stealer behaviour) Actions on Objectives Medium
Hunts the credential-collection burst pattern executed by the Nx Console v18.95.0 stealer: a single Code.exe or node.exe process touching five or more distinct credential/secret files (.env, ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.npmrc, ~/.kube/config, ~/.claude/settings.json, ~/.config/1Password) within a 5-minute window. The behaviour mirrors the published payload's documented target list across GitHub / npm / AWS / 1Password / HashiCorp Vault / Kubernetes / Anthropic Claude Code. Rationale: Implements the credential-harvest signature documented in the article (the payload 'read .env files') and corroborated by StepSecurity / nrwl postmortem (targets npm, GitHub, AWS, 1Password, Kubernetes, HashiCorp Vault, Anthropic Claude Code). The 5-distinct-paths-in-5-minutes threshold catches the burst behaviour while suppressing normal developer dotenv usage which typically touches 1-2 files. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/nx-console-vs-code-extension-compromised • https://nx.dev/blog/nx-console-v18-95-0-postmortem • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/compromised-nx-console-18950-targeted.html
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1555 T1083 T1539
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
let CredPathFragments = dynamic([@"\.aws\credentials", @"/.aws/credentials", @"\.npmrc", @"/.npmrc", @"\.kube\config", @"/.kube/config", @"\.claude\settings.json", @"/.claude/settings.json", @"\.config\1Password", @"/.config/1Password", @"\.docker\config.json", @"vault-token", @".gitconfig"]);
let CredFileNames = dynamic([".env",".envrc","credentials",".npmrc",".pypirc","settings.json","config","vault-token"]);
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","node","Code.exe","Code - Insiders.exe","Code Helper","Code Helper.exe")
| where (FolderPath has_any (CredPathFragments)) or (FileName in~ (CredFileNames) and FolderPath !contains "node_modules")
| summarize DistinctPaths = dcount(strcat(FolderPath, FileName)), SamplePaths = make_set(strcat(FolderPath, FileName), 25), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp), Cmd = any(InitiatingProcessCommandLine)
  by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessId, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 5m)
| where DistinctPaths >= 5
| order by FirstSeen desc
let CredPathFragments = dynamic([@"\.aws\credentials", @"/.aws/credentials", @".npmrc", @"\.kube\config", @"/.kube/config", @"\.claude\settings.json", @"/.claude/settings.json", @"\.config\1Password", @"/.config/1Password", @"\.docker\config.json", @"vault-token"]);
let CredFileNames = dynamic([".env",".envrc","credentials",".npmrc",".pypirc","settings.json","vault-token"]);
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("node.exe","node","Code.exe","Code - Insiders.exe","Code Helper")
| where (TargetFilePath has_any (CredPathFragments)) or (TargetFileName in~ (CredFileNames) and TargetFilePath !contains "node_modules")
| summarize DistinctPaths = dcount(TargetFilePath), SamplePaths = make_set(TargetFilePath, 25), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated), Cmd = any(ActingProcessCommandLine)
  by DvcHostname, ActingProcessId, ActingProcessName, ActorUsername, bin(TimeGenerated, 5m)
| where DistinctPaths >= 5
| order by FirstSeen desc
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 @Image:(*\\node.exe OR *\\Code.exe OR *\\Code\ -\ Insiders.exe OR *\\Code\ Helper.exe) @TargetFilename:(*\\.env OR *\\.envrc OR *\\.aws\\credentials OR *\\.npmrc OR *\\.kube\\config OR *\\.claude\\settings.json OR *\\.config\\1Password* OR *\\.docker\\config.json OR *vault-token*) -@TargetFilename:*\\node_modules\\*
(#event_simpleName=FileOpenInfo OR #event_simpleName=FileWritten)
| ContextImageFileName=/(node(\.exe)?|Code(\.exe)?|Code - Insiders\.exe|Code Helper(\.exe)?)$/i
| regex("\\\\\\.env$|\\\\\\.envrc$|\\\\\\.aws\\\\credentials|/\\.aws/credentials|\\\\\\.npmrc|/\\.npmrc|\\\\\\.kube\\\\config|/\\.kube/config|\\\\\\.claude\\\\settings\\.json|/\\.claude/settings\\.json|\\\\\\.config\\\\1Password|/\\.config/1Password|\\\\\\.docker\\\\config\\.json|vault-token", field=TargetFileName)
| TargetFileName!=/node_modules/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextProcessId, ContextImageFileName], function=count(as=distinct_hits))
| distinct_hits>=5

Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs Actions on Objectives High
Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.
ATT&CKT1539 T1555.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent

| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",
                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",
                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1", "43f2b001846c4966073ebffa5be8f15e491a1e7d32bbd805d57406ff540e0dd9") or SHA1 in~ ("1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1", "43f2b001846c4966073ebffa5be8f15e491a1e7d32bbd805d57406ff540e0dd9") or MD5 in~ ("1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1", "43f2b001846c4966073ebffa5be8f15e491a1e7d32bbd805d57406ff540e0dd9")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1", "43f2b001846c4966073ebffa5be8f15e491a1e7d32bbd805d57406ff540e0dd9") or SHA1 in~ ("1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1", "43f2b001846c4966073ebffa5be8f15e491a1e7d32bbd805d57406ff540e0dd9") or MD5 in~ ("1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1", "43f2b001846c4966073ebffa5be8f15e491a1e7d32bbd805d57406ff540e0dd9")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1", "43f2b001846c4966073ebffa5be8f15e491a1e7d32bbd805d57406ff540e0dd9"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).

[LLM] EchoCreep Discord API beacon from non-browser process (Webworm 2025) Command & Control High
Hunts the EchoCreep backdoor's Discord-based C2 channel: a script interpreter or non-browser process beaconing to discord.com / discordapp.com API endpoints to upload files, fetch jobs, and run cmd.exe shell commands. ESET decrypted 400+ Discord messages and four guild/channel pairs tied to this campaign. Rationale: Article anchors EchoCreep to Discord API calls for upload/download/shell/sleep (Table 1) and explicitly states the backdoor's network traffic 'passes through Discord APIs using crafted HTTP requests'. Excluding the genuine Discord client + browsers leaves only the C2 path. Cross-checked Mandiant's Discord-C2 pattern guidance to confirm exclusion list. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1102/002/ • https://www.symantec-enterprise-blogs.security.com/threat-intelligence/webworm-espionage-rats
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1102.002 T1059.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
let LookbackDays = 7d;
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("discord.com","discordapp.com","discord.gg","cdn.discordapp.com")
   or RemoteUrl has_any ("/api/v9/","/api/v10/")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe","iexplore.exe","Discord.exe","DiscordPTB.exe","DiscordCanary.exe","Spotify.exe","slack.exe","Teams.exe","ms-teams.exe","WebexTeams.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            FirstSeen = min(Timestamp),
            LastSeen = max(Timestamp),
            SampleUrl = any(RemoteUrl),
            SampleCmd = any(InitiatingProcessCommandLine),
            DistinctRemoteIPs = dcount(RemoteIP)
          by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath
| where ConnCount >= 3
| order by FirstSeen desc
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let RecentInterpreters = SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where EventID == 4688
    | where NewProcessName has_any ("\\powershell.exe","\\pwsh.exe","\\cmd.exe","\\cscript.exe","\\wscript.exe","\\rundll32.exe","\\regsvr32.exe","\\mshta.exe","\\curl.exe","\\wget.exe")
    | where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
    | project InterpreterTime=TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, NewProcessId;
let DiscordTraffic = ImNetworkSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where DstHostname has_any ("discord.com","discordapp.com","discord.gg","cdn.discordapp.com")
       or Url has_any ("/api/v9/","/api/v10/","discord.com/api","discordapp.com/api")
    | project NetTime=TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcUsername, SrcIpAddr, DstHostname, Url;
DiscordTraffic
| join kind=inner RecentInterpreters on $left.DvcHostname == $right.Computer
| where NetTime between (InterpreterTime .. InterpreterTime + 1h)
| summarize ConnCount=count(), FirstNet=min(NetTime), LastNet=max(NetTime), Interpreters=make_set(NewProcessName), SampleCmd=any(CommandLine), SampleUrl=any(Url)
        by DvcHostname, SubjectUserName, DstHostname
| where ConnCount >= 3
| order by FirstNet desc

[LLM] GraphWorm OneDrive /createUploadSession C2 from non-Office process Command & Control High
Hunts GraphWorm backdoor C2: Microsoft Graph API calls to /createUploadSession and victim-specific OneDrive directories from a non-Office, non-Edge process. ESET observed GraphWorm exclusively using OneDrive endpoints to fetch jobs and upload large staged files, with a separate directory per victim. Rationale: Article explicitly names the abused endpoint: 'the Microsoft Graph API endpoint /createUploadSession to upload large, staged files' and confines GraphWorm to OneDrive paths per-victim. Excluding native Office/OneDrive/Edge processes preserves the malicious signal while suppressing legit Graph use. Cross-referenced MITRE ATT&CK T1102.002 and Microsoft's Graph API consumer list. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1102/002/ • https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/driveitem-createuploadsession
ATT&CKT1102.002 T1567.002 T1071.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
let LookbackDays = 7d;
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where RemoteUrl has "graph.microsoft.com"
   and (RemoteUrl has "createUploadSession" or RemoteUrl has "/me/drive/items" or RemoteUrl has "/drives/" or RemoteUrl has "/me/drive/root:")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("msedge.exe","chrome.exe","firefox.exe","OneDrive.exe","OneDriveStandaloneUpdater.exe","Teams.exe","ms-teams.exe","WINWORD.EXE","EXCEL.EXE","POWERPNT.EXE","OUTLOOK.EXE","ONENOTE.EXE","Outlook.exe","officeclicktorun.exe","backgroundtaskhost.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            FirstSeen = min(Timestamp),
            LastSeen = max(Timestamp),
            SampleUrl = any(RemoteUrl),
            SampleCmd = any(InitiatingProcessCommandLine)
          by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath
| order by FirstSeen desc
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let RecentInterpreters = SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where EventID == 4688
    | where NewProcessName has_any ("\\powershell.exe","\\pwsh.exe","\\cmd.exe","\\rundll32.exe","\\regsvr32.exe","\\mshta.exe","\\cscript.exe","\\wscript.exe","\\curl.exe")
    | where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
    | project InterpreterTime=TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine;
let GraphTraffic = ImNetworkSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where DstHostname has "graph.microsoft.com"
       and (Url has "createUploadSession" or Url has "/me/drive/items" or Url has "/drives/" or Url has "/me/drive/root:")
    | project NetTime=TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcUsername, SrcIpAddr, DstHostname, Url;
GraphTraffic
| join kind=inner RecentInterpreters on $left.DvcHostname == $right.Computer
| where NetTime between (InterpreterTime .. InterpreterTime + 1h)
| summarize ConnCount=count(), FirstNet=min(NetTime), LastNet=max(NetTime), Interpreters=make_set(NewProcessName), SampleCmd=any(CommandLine), SampleUrl=any(Url)
        by DvcHostname, SubjectUserName, DstHostname
| order by FirstNet desc
